supporting_stories.topic: Valkyries and Dream complete sweeps to reach WNBA Finals
supporting_stories.headline: Valkyries and Dream sweep to WNBA Finals

tweets.text:
The 2026 WNBA Finals are set.

Golden State Valkyries vs Atlanta Dream

Who's taking home the trophy?

supporting_stories.research_notes:
Golden State Valkyries franchise history: 2025 53.2 W%, First Round Exit. 2026 72.7 W%, Finals Bound per StatMuse. That's a year-two leap. They are now the best playoff win percentage by a franchise all-time: 62.5%, ahead of Minnesota Lynx 58.9% and Houston Comets 58.8% per StatMuse. They joined the WNBA in 2025 and are about to play in the 2026 WNBA Finals per ClutchPoints — 'CRAZY!' per ClutchPoints.

A'ja Wilson vs Golden State Game 3: 21 PTS, 10 REB, 2 BLK, 6-19 FG — couldn't escape Valkatraz per StatMuse. The defending MVP and the league's best player was held to 6-19 shooting. The Aces — who have never been swept in the Coach Becky era per StatMuse — just got swept at home.

Angel Reese in Game 3 vs New York: 22 PTS, 9 REB, 3 AST, 2 BLK. Headed to her first WNBA Finals per StatMuse. 'I manifested this' per ESPN. Mom's been there every step of the way per ESPN. Jordin Canada: 19 PTS, 11 AST (0 TOV), 5-8 FG — ties Diana Taurasi for the fifth-most PTS/AST double-doubles in WNBA playoff history per StatMuse.

The Atlanta Dream have clinched their spot in the WNBA Finals per StatMuse — their first since 2013 per SportsCenter. DeWanna Bonner will play in her fifth WNBA Finals, tied for the third-most all-time per StatMuse.

Both the No. 1 seed (Aces) and the No. 3 seed (Liberty) were swept at home. The WNBA Finals are set: Golden State Valkyries vs Atlanta Dream per ESPN.

Gabby Williams in Game 3: 16 PTS, 3 AST, 3 STL — scored 0 at half, all 16 in the second half. 'You can say I was A.S.S' per WNBAonNBC. Williams hit the dagger jumper to seal it per ClutchPoints. Joe Lacob hit the 'night night' moments before the Valkyries advanced per ClutchPoints/HaterReport.

Total All-Star appearances by roster: 26 — Las Vegas Aces, 4 — Golden State Valkyries. Golden State gets the sweep per StatMuse.
supporting_stories.gif_concept: quiet vindication after being doubted all season — the Valkyries were an expansion team, the Dream were underdogs, and both just swept the reigning powers
supporting_stories.meme_concept: Valkyries and Dream are the hardened veterans now, having just dispatched the favorites — Aces and Liberty are the shocked newcomers who thought this would be easy

beats.angle: The Valkyries' historic leap — 53.2 W% first-round exit in Year 1 to 72.7 W% Finals Bound in Year 2, now best playoff win% in WNBA history
beats.landing: The reader understands this is not just a cinderella story; this is the fastest rise to dominance in league history

beats.angle: The Aces' historic fall — A'ja Wilson held to 6-19, swept for the first time in the Becky Hammon era, at home
beats.landing: The reader grasps the upset: the league's best player and the league's best coach just got swept by an expansion team

beats.angle: The Dream's return — Angel Reese's first Finals, Jordin Canada tying Taurasi, DeWanna Bonner's fifth Finals, Atlanta's first since 2013
beats.landing: The reader sees the legacy and the arrival: the Dream are back, and a new generation has taken over

supporting_stories.topic: Louisville demolishes Florida State 44-20 — Isaac Brown 235 rush yards, Mike Norvell's seat blazing
supporting_stories.headline: Louisville demolishes FSU 44-20 as Norvell's seat blazes
supporting_stories.research_notes:
Louisville beat Florida State 44-20 per ground truth — this is the Mike Norvell buyout/hot seat story finally hitting a breaking point.

Isaac Brown vs Florida State: 17 CAR, 235 YDS, 2 TD per StatMuse — the first Louisville player with 230 rushing yards in a game since Javian Hawkins in 2019 per StatMuse. That's the performance.

CBS Sports: 'How is Mike Norvell still employed? Buyout, leadership uncertainty keeping hot seat coach at Florida State.' Norvell's seat hasn't gotten any cooler, but Florida State has been hesitant to make a move per CBS Sports.

FSU is 0-13 outside Doak Campbell since missing the CFP in 2023 per RedditCFB. That's the stat that defines the collapse. They went 13-0 in 2023, got snubbed by the playoff, and have not won a single road game since.

W_B_Rick: 'Louisville is just fucking pitiful dude.' (This was posted during the game, so it's unclear if he meant Louisville or FSU, but given the score, he likely meant FSU.)

RedditCFB: 'FSU was looking really good up 14-0 tonight, but then they fell victim to a classic blunder: giving up 28 points in a row.' That's the collapse in miniature.

RedditCFB: 'Louisville is gonna be the best 2-10 team in the country.' (This is clearly a joke, but it captures the chaos.)

The question you answer: why hasn't FSU fired Norvell yet? Buyout and leadership uncertainty. But how long can that hold?
supporting_stories.gif_concept: quiet resignation as the season ends — Mike Norvell watching another blowout loss, knowing his seat is blazing but the buyout is too big

beats.angle: Isaac Brown's 235-yard demolition of FSU — Louisville ran through the Seminoles
beats.landing: The reader sees the dominance: Louisville physically overwhelmed FSU, and FSU had no answer

beats.angle: FSU is 0-13 outside Doak Campbell since the 2023 CFP snub — Norvell's seat is blazing, but the buyout and leadership uncertainty are keeping him employed
beats.landing: The reader understands the stalemate: FSU can't afford to fire Norvell, but they also can't afford to keep him

supporting_stories.topic: Pat McAfee Show announces Field Pass for Super Bowl, select MNF games, and CFP Season 5
supporting_stories.headline: McAfee Show getting Field Pass for Super Bowl, MNF, CFP
supporting_stories.research_notes:
The Pat McAfee Show announced they will OFFICIALLY be doing a Field Pass for the Super Bowl this year per PatMcAfeeShow — they will also be doing select Monday Night Football games per PatMcAfeeShow. 'This is an absolute honor' per PatMcAfeeShow.

Season 5 of Field Pass for the College Football Playoff will be happening per PatMcAfeeShow.

This is a big media-rights story disguised as a Pat McAfee announcement. ESPN is giving McAfee the Super Bowl and MNF Field Pass access — that's a signal of how much they value his brand and his reach. The CFP Field Pass was already a thing, but the Super Bowl is new. That's the headline.

The question you answer: why does this matter? Because McAfee is now the second screen for the biggest game of the year. He's not replacing the broadcast — he's the alternative broadcast, the one that's loose and fun and doesn't pretend to be objective. ESPN is betting that a chunk of the Super Bowl audience wants that.

beats.angle: McAfee getting Field Pass for the Super Bowl and select MNF games — ESPN giving him the biggest stage
beats.landing: The reader understands: McAfee is now the alternative broadcast for the Super Bowl, and ESPN is betting big on his reach
